name: seven-years
transcript: October 2019 to September 2026 Seven years in sixty seconds. The Center for Smart Cyber-Physical Systems at UMass Lowell Peer-reviewed papers, year by year: 2019: 4, 2020: 21, 2021: 22, 2022: 23, 2023: 37, 2024: 38, 2025: 44, 2026: 26. 2019 counts October to December, from the center's founding; 2026 counts through September. Who works with whom, year by year: the collaboration graph grows from 2019 to 2026 to 19 people and 29 working pairs. Milestones: 2019: the center is founded by five faculty; 2021: Vinod Vokkarane becomes director; 2024: ONR post-disaster restoration award, and the DOE CyberCARED consortium; 2026: NSF instrumentation award for SUMMIT, a three-university grid testbed; 2026: BOND-AI, printed electronics with industry partners. By the numbers: 215 peer-reviewed papers since 2019; $8.0M in awards the center led; 20 faculty in four colleges; 16 doctoral students today. Seven years in, and just getting started.. Sense. Communicate. Decide with people. Act. smartcyberphysical.org

name: paper-fusion
transcript: A paper in 30 seconds FUSION: A Unified Benchmarking Framework for Reproducible Optical Network Research. Journal of Optical Communications and Networking, 2026 The problem: Why it matters: Results in optical networking are getting harder to compare and reproduce: architectures now range from single-band to multi-band and space-division systems, and published numbers depend on simulation assumptions that are rarely spelled out. What we found: The result: Case studies show the framework benchmarking heterogeneous architectures and policies on equal terms, and a mapping of published studies onto FUSION's capabilities shows how much of the field's recent work it can already reproduce. Who: Authors: A. Rezaee, R. McCann, V. M. Vokkarane Read it: doi.org/10.1364/JOCN.593123 More research. Advanced Communication Networks Laboratory smartcyberphysical.org/acnl.html

name: paper-qot-grooming
transcript: A paper in 30 seconds QoT-Aware Dynamic Resource Allocation and Grooming in Multi-Band Space-Division Multiplexing Networks. Journal of Optical Communications and Networking, 2026 The problem: Why it matters: Multi-band space-division multiplexing can scale backbone capacity, but allocating resources dynamically means accounting for inter-core crosstalk, inter-channel stimulated Raman scattering, amplifier noise, and nonlinear interference at the same time, and their effects differ by band and by core count. What we found: The result: Ignoring frequency-dependent crosstalk causes systematic, band-dependent errors in which modulation formats are feasible in dense-core fibers. Who: Authors: A. Rezaee, F. Arpanaei, R. McCann, H. Rabbani, J. Hernández, M. Brandt-Pearce, V. M. Vokkarane Read it: doi.org/10.1364/JOCN.596435 More research. Advanced Communication Networks Laboratory smartcyberphysical.org/acnl.html

name: paper-spectral-spatial
transcript: A paper in 30 seconds QoT-Aware Spectral and Spatial Scaling Trade-offs in Multi-Band Space Division Multiplexing over EONs. Journal of Optical Communications and Networking, 2026 (invited) The problem: Why it matters: Backbone capacity can grow two ways, by adding bands beyond the C-band or by adding fiber cores, and physical-layer impairments mean the two cannot be judged separately: the L-band suffers more crosstalk, and dense cores make crosstalk dominate. What we found: The result: The best band plan depends on the core count. C+L wins for 4 and 7 cores; C+S wins for 13 cores because the L-band is hit harder by crosstalk; at 19 cores the system is crosstalk-dominated and only C+S holds up. Who: Authors: A. Rezaee, F. Arpanaei, R. McCann, L. Nadal, J. A. Hernández, V. M. Vokkarane Read it: doi.org/10.1364/JOCN.596854 More research. Advanced Communication Networks Laboratory smartcyberphysical.org/acnl.html

name: thrust-energy
transcript: Research thrust Resilient energy and infrastructure. What keeps the grid, a reactor, a highway, or a bridge working when the computers and networks that run it are attacked or knocked out, and how does it come back? Lines of work: Seeing the grid under attack; Restoring power and communication together; Nuclear energy and security; Transportation and civil infrastructure. Resilient energy and infrastructure. Co-leads: Sukesh Aghara and Yuanchang Xie smartcyberphysical.org/research-energy.html

name: thrust-networks
transcript: Research thrust Next-generation networks and trusted devices. How do you build networks that carry cyber-physical traffic at the speed AI needs, and devices at the edge that can be trusted? Lines of work: Multi-band and space-division optical networks; Fault-tolerant distributed and edge computing; Zero trust for cyber-physical systems; Printed electronics for hard places. Next-generation networks and trusted devices. Co-leads: Lewis Tseng and Orlando Arias smartcyberphysical.org/research-networks.html

name: thrust-cpai
transcript: Research thrust Cyber-physical AI. How does a system that senses the physical world turn what it senses into decisions it can be trusted to act on? Lines of work: Digital twins, sensing, and state recovery; Learning without moving the data; High-performance computing and data integrity; Agentic control within limits. Cyber-physical AI. Co-leads: Yan Luo and Seung Woo Son smartcyberphysical.org/research-cpai.html

name: thrust-people
transcript: Research thrust People in the loop. When a person and an AI share a decision about a system that can hurt someone, who decides what, and how do they learn to trust each other? Lines of work: Trust between people and robots; Ethics of algorithms that act; Decision-making under pressure; Education and workforce. People in the loop. Co-leads: Paul Robinette and Nicholas Evans smartcyberphysical.org/research-people.html

name: summit
transcript: NSF Major Research Instrumentation, Award #2511635 SUMMIT. One grid experiment across three universities The UMass Lowell main site, a wide-area software-defined network, and federation sites at NYU Tandon and West Virginia University. What it makes possible: Real-time simulation of the Northeast transmission grid; Control, networking, and cybersecurity hardware in the loop; Three universities federated over a wide-area network; Hardware-in-the-loop simulation offered as a service. SUMMIT at a glance: $2.0M NSF instrumentation award; 3 universities, one testbed; 4 Co-PIs with the PI at UMass Lowell. Built at UMass Lowell. October 2026 to September 2029 smartcyberphysical.org/summit.html

name: join-us
transcript: Ph.D. positions Build the systems the world runs on..
